summary: 46-year-old man, 6 days of RIF pain with a tender mass, fever 38.3 °C, WBC 16, CRP 210; CT shows perforated appendicitis with a 5.5 cm pericaecal abscess. Haemodynamically stable.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right iliac fossa pain and swelling for 6 days
inputs.hpi: 6 days of right lower abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus. Treated at home with paracetamol. For 2 days he has felt a tender lump in the right lower abdomen, with fevers and sweats. Eating a little, no vomiting. Bowels opened normally. No urinary symptoms. No weight loss, no rectal bleeding.

exam.abdomen: Tender 6 cm mass in the right iliac fossa with localised guarding. Rest of the abdomen soft, no generalised peritonism. Bowel sounds present.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Perforated appendicitis with a 5.5 × 4.8 cm rim-enhancing pericaecal abscess containing an appendicolith. No free intraperitoneal gas, no generalised free fluid. Caecal wall mildly thickened; no mass lesion seen.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Complicated appendicitis with periappendiceal abscess
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Complicated (perforated) appendicitis with a 5.5 cm pericaecal abscess — non-operative management with IV antibiotics and CT-guided percutaneous drainage.

socratesAnswers.associated: Fever, sweats and rigors, anorexia, tender lump

mustInclude.note: Complicated appendicitis with abscess always needs therapeutic antibiotics.

WSES 2020: non-operative management with antibiotics and percutaneous drainage (if available) is reasonable for a periappendiceal abscess; laparoscopic surgery in experienced hands is an alternative. Quality because both are acceptable.

dxVariant.proposedFix: Order the appendicitis variants from most to least specific (generalised peritonitis, abscess, phlegmon, localised peritonitis, uncomplicated) and remove the bare 'appendicitis' keyword from the uncomplicated variant (make it the fallback when no other variant matches).

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Clinical scores (AIR/AAS over Alvarado), imaging by age/sex/pregnancy, antibiotic-first option, complicated appendicitis (abscess), antibiotic duration
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S, Podda M, De Simone B, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:27.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — international guidelines for sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening (do not use qSOFA alone), antibiotics within 1 h of shock, blood cultures, lactate, 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypoperfusion, vasopressors, source control
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: late presentation with a periappendiceal abscess. Tests that the plan changes to antibiotics plus drainage (or experienced laparoscopic surgery), keeps interval colon evaluation for a patient over 40, and that the Plan-tab variant follows the assessment ('abscess') rather than defaulting to uncomplicated disease.
